newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian government crisis as minister investigated.
newsitem.headline: Belgian government crisis as minister investigated.

text.p: The Belgian government slid towards crisis on Tuesday as leaders of the parliamentary parties decided to set up a commission to study allegations that Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo had sex with minors.
Several leaders said Di Rupo, a francophone Socialist who angrily rejects the accusations which first surfaced in Dutch-language newspapers at the weekend, might be forced to resign.
"Parliament will meet at 4.00 p.m. (1500 GMT) today to decide on the make-up of the commission," Parliament Chairman Raymond Langendries told reporters after the meeting.

The special commission will study the allegations against Di Rupo and decide whether to recommend to the full parliament to lift his immunity from prosecution and whether he should appear before the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's top court.
Di Rupo earlier told reporters he had requested the move which would allow him to see the allegations against him which he says are baseless and politically motivated.
"I repeat for the umpteenth time that I have never been involved in paedophilia. What is happening now to me really seems like political scheming," he told reporters.
Di Rupo has not denied in his statements that he is a homosexual but says his private life is his own and he has only ever had sexual relations with consenting adults.

Didier Reynders, head of the opposition francophone Liberal parliamentary party, said the Brussels public prosecutor had given the leaders a document stating there were "sufficient indications" to open an investigation into Di Rupo.
"If parliament refers Di Rupo to the Cassation I do not see how he could...remain in office," he told reporters.
The commission, which could make its recommendation within days, will be made up of 11 people -- seven from the ruling centre-left coalition and four from opposition parties.
"If he is referred to the Cour de Cassation...it would be difficult for him to retain his position as a deputy prime minister," Paul Tant, CVP parliamentary leader said earlier.
The Flemish CVP Christian Democratic Party is the largest party in the ruling coalition government.
Belgium's coalition government is made up of the francophone and Flemish Christian democratic and socialist parties.
Herman de Croo, leader of the main Dutch-speaking opposition VLD Liberals said Di Rupo should quit regardless.

The government of the French-speaking Walloon region also said on Tuesday it had set up an inquiry into Jean-Pierre Grafe, the French Community's minister for higher education, who also faces allegations of under-age sex -- charges he denies.

The parliamentary process instituted against Di Rupo echoes that used against Flemish socialist and NATO secretary-general Willy Claes, who was forced to resign as head of the alliance last year when his immunity was lifted in the face of allegations he knew of a party slush fund in the 1980s.
Political analysts say the government is not under immediate threat, but the key will be whether Flemish and francophone Christian Democrats support Di Rupo or quietly back off.

Their failure to support the socialist politician could spell the eventual end of the coalition, at a time when public confidence in the whole political apparatus and in the socialist parties in particular is already at a very low ebb.

Last month 250,000 people took to the streets of Brussels in a march originally called to support parents of missing and murdered children in the paedophile scandal that has rocked Belgium, which turned into a show of public disgust at what is seen as a thoroughly corrupt political and legal system.
